title: Aspect — The Core Concept
grammarPoint: Perfective vs. imperfective aspect: completed single event vs. ongoing/habitual/repeated action

explanation.text:
Polish verbs come in pairs: **imperfective** (niedokonany) and **perfective** (dokonany).

**The key distinction:**

| Imperfective | Perfective |
|--------------|------------|
| Action ongoing, habitual, or repeated | Action completed, single event |
| Process matters | Result matters |
| All tenses possible | No present tense* |
| e.g. pisać | e.g. napisać |

*Perfective verbs have no true present tense — their present-looking forms are actually future!

**When to use each:**

**Imperfective (niedokonany):**
- Habitual: Codziennie **czytałem** gazetę. (I read the newspaper every day — routine)
- Duration/process: **Pisałem** list przez godzinę. (I was writing a letter for an hour)
- Background action: Kiedy **spałem**, zadzwonił telefon. (While I was sleeping, the phone rang)

**Perfective (dokonany):**
- Single completed event: Wczoraj **przeczytałem** książkę. (Yesterday I read [finished] the book)
- Achieved result: W końcu **napisałem** list. (I finally wrote [and finished] the letter)

**Common aspect pairs:**

| Imperfective | Perfective | English |
|-------------|------------|--------|
| pisać | napisać | to write |
| czytać | przeczytać | to read |
| robić | zrobić | to do/make |
| kupować | kupić | to buy |
| mówić | powiedzieć | to say |
notes: Every Polish verb belongs to an aspect pair — learn them together.
Perfective verbs CANNOT be used in present tense — their present form = future!
'Piszę' (I write/am writing) — imperfective. 'Napiszę' (I will write) — perfective future.

exercises.prompt: Codziennie ___ kawę rano. (Every day I drink coffee in the morning.) Which aspect is correct?
exercises.explanation: 'Codziennie' (every day) signals habitual action → imperfective: piłem. 'Wypiłem' would mean 'I drank up [finished] the coffee' — one completed event.

exercises.prompt: W końcu ___ to zadanie domowe. (I finally finished the homework.) [zrobić vs. robić]
exercises.explanation: 'W końcu' (finally) + completed result → perfective: zrobiłem. 'Robiłem' would mean I was doing it (process, not completion).

exercises.prompt: Kiedy ___ (I was reading — imperfective), zadzwoniła mama. (While I was reading, mum called.)
exercises.hint: Background ongoing action (while...) = imperfective past: czytać → czytałem/czytałam

exercises.explanation: You heard: 'Wczoraj przeczytałem całą książkę.' — Yesterday I read [finished] the whole book. Perfective 'przeczytać' → completed event.

exercises.prompt: Which statement about perfective verbs is TRUE?
options: They have no true present tense
They are less common than imperfective
They only exist in past tense
exercises.explanation: Perfective verbs CANNOT express present tense — their present-looking form is actually future. E.g., 'napiszę' = I WILL write (future), not 'I write'.
